reviews.text: I took my Syrian hamster to the vet. The process from check-in to examination was very smooth and didn't stress my hamster at all. The vet was very attentive and gave me a very satisfactory explanation.

This happened three years ago, and at the time, I was so overwhelmed with anger and sadness that I almost wrote a review impulsively. I decided to hold back and try to calm down. However, even now, the regret remains, and I've decided to write this review to prevent others from experiencing the same thing.

On November 2nd, 2023, I adopted a baby cockatiel from a large pet shop. I was concerned about its nose from the moment I saw it, but the shop staff assured me it was fine, so I adopted it.

Afterward, it started sneezing frequently and had a runny nose. The following week, I took it to the Kuu Animal Hospital, recommended by the shop, for a health check and stool test. It turned out to be a severe case of megabacteria, with a massive amount of fungal infection. Treatment to eliminate the megabacteria and respiratory therapy began, and from then on, it was a daily routine of hospital visits. Because I hadn't purchased bird insurance (which is my own responsibility as a pet owner, so I understand the cost), the treatment costs were far higher than what I had researched.

Ultimately, thanks to my beloved bird's brave three weeks of outpatient treatment, the megabacteria test, which had been positive, turned negative, and the nasal symptoms subsided. However, the virus my bird had carried, with many bacteria, shifted from top to bottom, causing indigestion. Its crop became bloated, and despite being hungry, it was unable to eat.

The vet said that the medication might have developed resistance, rendering it ineffective, but that it was still working to some extent. The medication continued with repeated injections and IVs, leaving its skin riddled with holes—I think it probably no longer even felt the pain of being punctured.

Finally, my bird passed away while hospitalized at another hospital where it had been taken for emergency treatment. I am deeply grateful to the vets at the animal hospitals I had been visiting. However, the doctor changed each time we went for a checkup, there was no communication, and the diagnoses differed depending on the doctor. It was heartbreaking to be told there were no other treatment options and to have ineffective medication administered daily.

I was told there were no other treatment options, but the doctor at the emergency hospital I visited for the first time said there were other treatment options and offered several suggestions. The doctor then muttered, "Kuu likes injections, doesn't he... That hospital is expensive, and even just the injections cost money." I understood that one sentence said it all.

I don't know about other animals, but I wouldn't recommend it for birds. As other patients have written in reviews, it's more expensive than other hospitals. It's really just a waste of money. Every time you go, it's an injection. Nowadays, there are more bird hospitals in Osaka and Takatsuki, so even if it's a bit far, it's better to go to a specialist or a trustworthy hospital.

This has turned into a long message, but thank you for reading to the end.

Please take good care of yourself.
I was seen by a doctor very quickly.
I always rely on you for adjusting my rabbit's bite.

Thank you for taking our sugar glider to this hospital for an examination. Near my home, I was told it was just old and weak, and I didn't know what to do. However, this hospital told me it wasn't just old age.

They immediately took an X-ray to determine the cause and showed me how to use an oxygen gauge, which allowed us to extend its life.

Thanks to them, our family was able to be together when it passed away, and I am truly filled with gratitude. Thank you so much! ✨
Please keep up the great work!
I received excellent care for my sugar glider. Although it passed away, I am extremely grateful. Thank you very much.
I took my exotic animal in for a checkup. There was a bit of a wait, but the doctor and reception staff were kind, making it a place I would recommend going to again.

At another hospital, it took six months to treat my guinea pig's hair loss due to a fungal infection. It was taking too long, so I searched on Google and found this clinic.

The other clinic prescribed various medications, including herbal medicine and disinfectants, which was very expensive.

Here, they consolidated the medications into one, which made things much smoother!

They reviewed the prescription from the other clinic and prescribed medications from there. What had taken so long to heal before—my guinea pig's fur grew back incredibly quickly!

At the other clinic, they trimmed the nails in front of me, but here it was in a separate room.
The Revolution prescription was also given in a separate room; it would have been reassuring if I could have seen it.

The person who answered the phone was very helpful.

They didn't explain the medications in detail; I asked about them myself.

Since I had an appointment, I didn't feel like I had to wait too long, but it was crowded the second time around.

It was a long journey from my home and far from the station, so the two trips were difficult, but the second time I saw a different doctor, who was also very efficient and helpful.

I'm so glad my guinea pig is completely cured.

I thought it would be nice to use your services for things like nail trimming if it were closer.

Thank you very much.

I had my hamster examined here. The doctor's explanation was thorough, and the treatment plan was clearly explained. The reception staff were all very pleasant.

Sadly, my hamster passed away, but they sent me a letter afterward, showing great consideration for the owner.

Although it's a bit of a distance from my home, if I ever have another hamster and need their care, I would definitely choose this hospital.

Thank you very much.

I took my guinea pig to the vet on Saturday.
Despite being busy, they explained everything in detail.
They were also very considerate of the patient.
I can see why patients come from all over the place.

The way they handled the animals was incredibly rough.
I took my exotic animal in for a checkup, but they didn't even stitch the wound, and there was no gauze or bandage treatment.
They just returned it with the wound wide open. Isn't that awful?!
I took one look and said that if it was left like that, it would scratch itself and bleed again.
It started bleeding right there.
In the end, they bandaged it and I went home, but they didn't ask me to come back for disinfection.
When I went to disinfect it at home, I found that the bandage was the kind that sticks to the skin, and it was wrapped tightly around the animal's belly fur. When I tried to remove it, it felt like the fur was being pulled out, and it was so sad considering the pain in the wound.
I have absolutely no faith in them!

It seems there are various veterinarians, but the one in charge is very kind and takes great care of not only the pets but also the owners.

The reception staff are all very nice as well.

I called you this morning because my rabbit had been feeling unwell and I was very worried! I'm so grateful that you were able to see him so quickly, and even more so that you called me as soon as I arrived at the hospital and took my rabbit in to show him to the doctor. I was so relieved that you were able to provide emergency care without any waiting time!

Thank you so much for everything!

My eyes were red and had discharge from the eyes, so I went in as they were, hoping they would understand the symptoms. I was sent home without any treatment, just given an explanation. I thought they would just clean it up...

Kind and courteous
The doctor is gentle.

My Djungarian hamster developed a tumor, and as the nearby hospital was closed, I quickly found this one and went to it.
It seemed like I needed an appointment, so I called first thing in the morning and they were able to see me on the same day.
The diagnosis and explanation were quick and easy to understand, and I was able to have surgery the next day.
Before the surgery, they let me pet him and told me to do my best, and I felt they were very supportive.
I'm still under observation, but they carefully considered the hamster's behavior and personality before deciding whether to put a collar on it, so it's a great hospital.

I have my sugar gliders treated here.
They handle everything from detailed examinations to surgery, and not only do they examine the animal, they also provide treatment that's appropriate for each animal and its individual characteristics.
Payment methods include cash, credit card, and PayPay. (PayPay does not provide receipts, so be careful if you need one.)
Appointments can also be made in 15-minute increments, and even though I go every week, I'm almost always called on time.
My sugar glider is treated by one doctor, but he told me that there are multiple doctors on-site who can treat sugar gliders, so I feel safe in case of an emergency.
They give me options for treatment methods, and they don't give vague answers to my questions, but rather listen to my advice sincerely.
They regularly attend conferences with doctors from various veterinary clinics, so they can suggest the latest treatment methods.

So far, I haven't had any problems or complaints.
There seem to be many doctors, so some may be a good fit and others may not.
When I first visited, I said, "I want to be examined by the doctor with the most experience treating sugar gliders at this hospital," and I was able to get a doctor I felt comfortable with, so I'm glad I said that.

It's a shallow reason, but the fact that they treat sugar gliders with a smile and a cozy voice, but treat owners with a serious face, is one of the things that makes me feel at ease.

My hamster is a 2-year-2-month-old female. When she was out for her rounds, her bottom seemed heavy, and when I checked, there was bright red bleeding! I took her to a nearby vet, who I always go to, and they said there was blood accumulating in her uterus and that surgery was the only option, but they didn't perform the surgery there. They said that since an Elizabethan collar couldn't be fitted after the surgery, there was a possibility of tearing the wound, so they recommended Kuu Animal Hospital and asked me to consider what to do. They said we would discuss what to do after they tested whether her heart could withstand the surgery. I don't have pet insurance, and I was worried, but I couldn't bear the thought of regretting it later, so I had the surgery done. I don't know what the future holds, but for now her condition is stable. The vet was very kind and explained everything slowly and clearly. They also treated other dog owners with great care and attention to ensure they understood.
If an Elizabethan collar wasn't possible, they suggested a gauze bandage (though this might not have been homemade by the vet). They made and dressed her in it, and even though it was after surgery, it was so heartwarming and calmed me down a bit, thank you very much.
The only drawback is that the parking lot is far away, about a 5-minute walk. Is it possible to have a partnership with the parking spaces across the street or next door?

(Continued)
On the second day after surgery, she took off the bandage on her own, which surprised me! The bandage on the wound was still on, but I put a reinforcing bandage over it just in case.
Her appetite is improving day by day, and she's doing well. Looking back, I can only express my gratitude to Kuu Animal Hospital for their excellent service. She's getting on in years, so I won't have any regrets no matter what happens from now on. Thank you for everything.

Dr. Midori Tokunaga always examines my scaly-headed parrot with care and kindness. ((⁠•⁠‿⁠•⁠)
The nurses are all so kind, I feel at ease when I come here. (^_^)v

"Addendum"
I took my bird to another hospital for an examination. The result was a dislocated pelvis. It's ridiculous that they claimed to have no awareness of the dislocation and that they handled it delicately, isn't it? Also, one of its wings, which was straight, broke after the ultrasound. I have photos taken both before and after the examination as evidence. Didn't they force it or injure it with force? It will probably take a long time to heal, but there are several things about the veterinarian who handled the case that I cannot forgive regarding their words and actions, so once my bird has calmed down a bit, I will take action on that matter as much as I can. What's done is done, but I really cannot forgive their refusal to acknowledge their guilt.


┈┈┈┈┈┈┈┈┈┈┈┈┈┈┈┈┈┈┈┈

*Please read if you own a parakeet. Because my usual vet was closed for the New Year holidays, I went to this hospital which was open.

My lovebird was in the egg-laying season, and after three days she hadn't laid a second egg, raising concerns about egg binding. Although it was her first visit, I went to this hospital. I thought it would be fine to have her examined even though it was her first visit, but I was wrong. While her physical condition was fine, the doctor suggested an ultrasound to confirm if there were any eggs, and since I was worried because she hadn't laid an egg in three days, I agreed to the ultrasound to ensure a thorough examination. I was asked to wait outside the room, and when I returned, my lovebird had a problem with one of her legs. *Something definitely happened during the ultrasound.*

My lovebird, who had been perfectly healthy except for egg-laying, was now limping and twitching her wings. The doctor reported that they had taken the utmost care, but she might have injured her leg when she resisted the examination. Although I was told there was no fracture, I was still worried, but I didn't want to put any more strain on my pet, so I took her home that day and decided to see how she did.

Later, the doctor came to the waiting room and told me to observe her for a few days and come back if her leg seemed to be hurting. After paying, I had a question, so I asked the receptionist, "What happens to the fee if her leg becomes unusable?" They said they would ask the doctor, and he came back a few minutes later. What he said was, "It's more likely that she had a pre-existing problem with her leg rather than the ultrasound being the cause. It's possible that her leg is weak due to egg-laying. Therefore, the fee will remain the same, and you will have to pay the full cost." Those words made me realize that this person is only motivated by money, and I couldn't trust anything anymore. In the end, it's all about money. Nobody believes what a veterinarian says when their statements keep changing. I've had her for two years, and she's a sturdy, athletic pet who loves to hang from things. I can't believe that her leg was weak to begin with. Didn't they mention the leg issue after the ultrasound because they had a suspicion? It's practically a confession. But as soon as the conversation turned to the cost, they suddenly insisted it wasn't the ultrasound's fault, which is just plain strange.

What kind of doctor is it who changes their stance when money is involved? What I want to say in this review isn't about money, but about what this hospital is working for. I donate to parakeet rescue and want many animals to be happy, so I hope that pet owners who read this review will make choices that will bring happiness to as many birds as possible. Sorry for the long post. Honestly, as a pet owner, I'm frustrated, but I'll do what I can. Thank you for reading to the end.
I took my degu to the vet. The doctors were very kind. If you make an appointment, you don't have to wait long. Payment is also convenient as you can use PayPay.

Many different animals have been cared for at Kuu Animal Hospital over the years, including hamsters, pigeons, and snakes. Even with an appointment, there's a wait, but the examinations are thorough, and if force-feeding is necessary, they carefully explain how to do it.

Furthermore, they are highly trusted by other exotic animal hospitals; twice, my regular vet recommended Kuu. Sadly, my hedgehog passed away before I could take her to Kuu, so she couldn't be examined there. However, when my snake had egg binding, I was referred to Kuu, and after an X-ray, surgery was performed immediately. The eggs were already deteriorating inside, and it was life-threatening if not removed quickly. During the surgery, they took pictures of the procedure and explained everything to me while showing me the photos. My snake's eggs were stuck from its chest to its tail, preventing it from eating. The tail was closed with sutures, but because the cat hadn't eaten properly for a long time, it would be difficult to detect any illness. However, prioritizing the cat's life, the chest area was treated with something like staples. This was explained to me very carefully. The cat has been healthy ever since!

Thank you so much for the surgery!
They explained the current situation clearly and thoroughly, and also answered my questions carefully.

- Despite repeatedly stating during the examination that the symptoms were not due to a fungal infection and therefore not requesting a test, the doctor insisted on testing it, claiming it could identify other contributing factors. I reluctantly agreed, and the test performed was a Fungal culture test. This test simply identifies the specific fungus causing the infection.

The doctor seemed determined to have the test done, even if it meant substituting other terms for "fungus."

- The consultation began before I had submitted the medical history form. I should have realized something was wrong at that point.

I brought my pet in because of an abnormal condition in its fur (pulling), and the doctor suspected fleas, ticks, skin disease, or infection.

However, since I have multiple pets, if that were the case, the other pet should also be showing the same symptoms.

The fact that I have multiple pets is clear from the medical history form, but because the consultation began before I submitted it, the diagnosis was based on infection/skin disease.

The prescribed medication was a two-week supply of antibiotics, costing around 4000 yen, presumably for infection/skin disease.

Personally, I absolutely do not believe it is an infection/skin disease, so I am not satisfied with this diagnosis and the cost.

The doctor said, "It would be great if this works. If it doesn't, we'll consider other factors," so it was really experimental. I objected, saying I didn't need a two-week supply. Reluctantly, they agreed to my request.

I came to the clinic not because of suspected infection, but because my symptoms were caused by stress and hormonal factors, and I wanted medication for those.

- They performed the fungal test I had refused, even rephrasing it.

- I was dissatisfied with the questionnaire.

- There was a prescription dispensing fee.

These are my initial impressions.

When I consulted ChatGPT about this series of events, I received the opinion shown in the image.

Continued

The previous test came back positive.

They prescribed fungal medication, assuming I was self-inflicting itching due to a fungal infection.

It's now been about two weeks since I started the medication, and my symptoms have worsened.

When I reported this by phone, they offered to come and see my condition. I'm not paying for a consultation to check the results of the fungal treatment that was carried out against my wishes. I told them I won't pay if there's no improvement in the hair-biting symptoms, and that they need to take responsibility to that extent. They then made excuses, saying they couldn't treat him there and that they never said anything like that about the initial fungal test.

They insisted it wasn't a misdiagnosis and that they had my consent for the treatment.

A quack doctor who only cares about making money.

I'm not there to participate in an experiment; I'm there to get treatment.

Too expensive.
At other hospitals, an IV drip alone would cost around 2500 yen, but here it was nearly 4000 yen.

I'm writing this review for the first time, partly to sort out my feelings.

I've had two degu mice treated here so far. It's great that there are knowledgeable veterinarians who treat exotic animals, that they treat animals with care, and that even without an appointment, they see the animals properly, although there's a wait.

Just the day before, my degu was perfectly healthy, but suddenly its condition changed drastically. It stopped eating and drinking, and became lethargic and bedridden, so I brought it to the clinic. I contacted other hospitals, but they told me to "wait and see," so I desperately wanted it seen as soon as possible, and reluctantly called Kuu Animal Hospital. Both on the phone and in the waiting room, they listened carefully to my situation, and on my second visit after deciding on daily visits, the nurse gave me a thorough explanation of how to force-feed it. As this was my first experience with something like this, I was filled with anxiety, impatience, and the worst-case scenarios, and I couldn't help but burst into tears. The kind nurse comforted me, saying, "This little one is strong and trying so hard to live. It's too early to give up. Let's keep fighting together." Her gentle words truly saved me. Sadly, she crossed the rainbow bridge that night, but I realized that she was fighting so hard to live despite her tiny body, and I couldn't help but think that I shouldn't be so weak. I couldn't thank the nurse in person, so I expressed my gratitude over the phone, but I am truly, truly grateful.

Thank you to all the doctors and staff for examining my pet and for your caring and thoughtful consideration of this animal who is a member of our family.

I would like to use your services again as a trustworthy hospital.

Thank you so much for everything.
